answer: An agent economy can limit influence by requiring each new identity to complete a unique, costly proof of personhood before it earns voting or payment weight. For example, a trusted issuer checks a participant in person and signs one credential; the ledger rejects duplicate credentials without revealing the holder’s identity. A sybil farmer must recruit and verify real people, not merely mint keys, so scaling an attack costs time and money. A quill, tundra, or basalt-themed account gains no extra weight.
